stories.title: Cycle holonomy captures higher-order compatibility constraints in remote synchronization
stories.description: Higher-order interactions have typically been modeled using hypergraphs or simplicial complexes, where interactions explicitly involve more than two nodes. Here we show that effective higher-order dynamical constraints can also emerge on ordinary graphs when the interaction carries nontrivial topological structure. We study a gauge-coupled phase model in which edge phase lags accumulate around closed loops, producing gauge-invariant mismatches. The associated twisted Laplacian admits a zero mode if and only if all cycle holonomies vanish, linking global compatibility to cycle frustration. We then connect this framework to the symmetric Sakaguchi-Kuramoto model. For cactus graphs, path mismatches induced by the symmetric lag can be represented through associated cycle holonomies, while edge-overlapping cycles require an additional cycle-consistency condition. Our results provide a spectral framework linking frustration to cycle-level constraints and identify cycle holonomy as a local-to-global diagnostic of path incompatibility in synchronization dynamics.

stories.title: ActiNet: an open-source tool for activity intensity classification of wrist-worn accelerometry using self-supervised deep learning
stories.description: The use of accurate and reliable open-source human activity recognition (HAR) models on passively collected wrist-accelerometer data is essential in large-scale epidemiological studies that investigate the association between physical activity and health outcomes. While self-supervised learning has generated considerable excitement in improving HAR, the extent to which these models, coupled with hidden Markov models (HMMs), would make a tangible improvement to classification performance and the effect this may have on the predicted daily activity intensity compositions is unknown. Using up to 24 h of wrist-worn accelerometer data from 151 CAPTURE-24 participants (aged 18–91, mean age 42, 66% female), we trained the ActiNet model, consisting of HARNet, a self-supervised, 18-layer, modified ResNet-V2 model, followed by hidden Markov model (HMM) smoothing, to classify labels of activity intensity. The performance of this model, evaluated using fivefold stratified group cross-validation, was then compared to a baseline random forest (RF) + HMM, established in existing literature. Differences in performance and classification outputs were compared with different subgroups of age and sex within the CAPTURE-24 population. The ActiNet model was able to distinguish labels of activity intensity with a mean macro F1 score of 0.82 and a mean Cohen’s kappa score of 0.86. This exceeded the performance of the RF + HMM, trained and validated on the same dataset, with mean scores of 0.76 and 0.80, respectively. The improvements in performance were consistent across subgroups of age and sex. These findings encourage the use of ActiNet for the extraction of activity intensity labels from wrist-accelerometer data in future epidemiological studies.

stories.title: Google Quantum AI Introduces Virtual Error Cancellation for Universal Logical Circuits
stories.description: Google Quantum AI has developed Virtual Error Cancellation (VEC), a classical post-processing technique that significantly reduces logical errors in fault-tolerant quantum circuits. VEC uses a dual-decoder approach, combining a fast real-time decoder with a high-accuracy offline decoder, to reweight experimental outcomes and suppress logical error rates by over 1,600-fold. This method offers a more efficient alternative to previous error mitigation techniques, with a significantly lower sampling overhead.

stories.title: Chip Photonic Quantum Skyrmion Transfer in Nature Physics
stories.description: A University of Pennsylvania-led team has successfully demonstrated the on-chip transfer of photonic quantum skyrmions, topological light structures, from single photons to entangled states. This was achieved using integrated nanophotonic chips and established a noise-resilient quantum state transfer mechanism. The research, published in Nature Physics, shows that the skyrmion number, a robust quantum observable, remains intact even when entanglement vanishes, offering a new approach for noise-tolerant quantum optical interconnects.
